page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-8-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core on a dedicated basis. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. Additionally, the instance is equipped with a bundled 402 GB local NVMe SSD for high-speed local storage, though it does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals a mix of performance characteristics. The instance exhibits strong single-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 2863.28 and a Geekbench text processing score of 2458.0, both placing in the top 25 percent. Multi-core performance and general computational tasks, such as software compilation and image processing, fall within the average range. However, significant memory bandwidth bottlenecks exist. While small-block cached read bandwidth is average at 565.78 GB/sec, large-block uncached read bandwidth drops to a weak 36.05 GB/sec, and large-block write bandwidth is poor at 13.63 GB/sec. LLM inference capabilities are average for small models but drop to weak performance when processing prompts on medium 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3d-standard-8-lssd offers a balanced hardware profile for workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources and fast local storage without the premium of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. The inclusion of a 402 GB local NVMe SSD provides high-speed, low-latency storage directly attached to the instance, making it highly suitable for database operations, static web serving, and general-purpose applications. However, the poor large-block memory write bandwidth suggests it is less optimal for memory-intensive data streaming or large-scale ETL pipelines. It is best suited for web serving, text processing, software development, and moderate database workloads.
